captions.text: Vitamin D is produced by our own bodies.
It's not really a vitamin, it's a hormone
that our skin produces when sunlight falls on our skin.
We spend all day inside, and when we do go outside,
we got a hat on, we got sleeves on, we got sunscreen on.
And as a result, very little ultraviolet light from the sun is falling on our skin,
and a lot of people have really low vitamin D levels.
If you are gonna have any blood tests done,
get your vitamin D level checked.
And if it's down in your boots, if it's five or eight or whatever,
you'd be wise to take 2,000 international units of vitamin D daily.
And that's a safe dose really for everybody.
